meta.title: Article Runner
meta.description: Production-oriented grammar data for a lane-based English article learning game.

ruleCatalog.label: First Mention: a / an
ruleCatalog.summary: Use 'a' or 'an' to introduce one nonspecific singular countable noun for the first time.

ruleCatalog.label: Jobs and Roles: a / an
ruleCatalog.summary: Use 'a' or 'an' with singular professions and roles, for example 'She is a teacher.'

ruleCatalog.label: Specific Nouns: the
ruleCatalog.summary: Use 'the' when the noun is identifiable, because both speakers know it or a phrase points to exactly which one it is.

ruleCatalog.label: Unique Things: the
ruleCatalog.summary: Use 'the' with things there is only one of, such as the sun, the moon and the internet.

ruleCatalog.label: Second Mention: the
ruleCatalog.summary: Use 'the' when a noun that was already introduced with 'a' or 'an' is mentioned again.

ruleCatalog.label: Meals: no article
ruleCatalog.summary: Use no article with meal names like breakfast, lunch and dinner in general expressions about daily routines.

ruleCatalog.label: Sports: no article
ruleCatalog.summary: Use no article with the names of sports, for example 'We play football.'

ruleCatalog.label: Languages: no article
ruleCatalog.summary: Use no article with the names of languages, for example 'They speak Arabic.'

ruleCatalog.label: Superlatives: the
ruleCatalog.summary: Use 'the' before superlative expressions such as the best, the tallest and the most interesting.

ruleCatalog.label: Ordinal Numbers: the
ruleCatalog.summary: Use 'the' before ordinal numbers such as first, second and third when they mark a definite position.

ruleCatalog.label: Rivers, Seas and Oceans: the
ruleCatalog.summary: Use 'the' with the names of rivers, seas, oceans and channels, for example the Nile and the Atlantic Ocean.

ruleCatalog.label: General Plurals: no article
ruleCatalog.summary: Use no article when plural countable nouns stand for a whole category in general, for example 'Trains are often late.'

ruleCatalog.label: General Uncountable: no article
ruleCatalog.summary: Use no article when an uncountable noun such as water, coffee or advice is used in a general sense.

ruleCatalog.label: Musical Instruments: the
ruleCatalog.summary: Use 'the' in standard expressions involving playing musical instruments, such as 'She plays the piano.'

ruleCatalog.label: Institutions for Purpose: no article
ruleCatalog.summary: Use no article in expressions such as 'at school' or 'go to school' when referring to the institution's normal purpose.

questions.sentence: I saw ___ dog near the park yesterday.
questions.explanation: Use 'a' because the dog is one nonspecific dog mentioned for the first time, and 'dog' starts with a consonant sound.
questions.completedSentence: I saw a dog near the park yesterday.

questions.sentence: She ate ___ apple before going to school.
questions.explanation: Use 'an' because 'apple' begins with a vowel sound, and this is the first time we hear about the apple.
questions.completedSentence: She ate an apple before going to school.

questions.sentence: Take ___ umbrella with you because it is raining.
questions.explanation: Use 'an' because 'umbrella' begins with a vowel sound; it means any umbrella, not one specific umbrella.
questions.completedSentence: Take an umbrella with you because it is raining.

questions.sentence: My parents bought ___ house last year.
questions.explanation: Use 'a' because the house is being introduced for the first time and is not yet identified for the listener.
questions.completedSentence: My parents bought a house last year.

questions.sentence: My sister is ___ teacher at our local school.
questions.explanation: Singular professions always take an indefinite article, and 'teacher' starts with a consonant sound, so we say 'a teacher'.
questions.completedSentence: My sister is a teacher at our local school.

questions.sentence: He wants to be ___ engineer when he grows up.
questions.explanation: Jobs take 'a' or 'an', and 'engineer' begins with a vowel sound even though it is spelled with 'e', so 'an' is correct.
questions.completedSentence: He wants to be an engineer when he grows up.

questions.sentence: Sara works as ___ nurse in London.
questions.explanation: Use 'a' because 'nurse' is a singular job, and the consonant sound 'n' at the start requires 'a', not 'an'.
questions.completedSentence: Sara works as a nurse in London.

questions.sentence: Her cousin is ___ actor in Hollywood.
questions.explanation: Use 'an' because 'actor' is a singular profession that begins with a vowel sound.
questions.completedSentence: Her cousin is an actor in Hollywood.

questions.sentence: Can you pass me ___ salt, please?
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the salt is right there on the table, so both speakers know exactly which salt is meant.
questions.completedSentence: Can you pass me the salt, please?

questions.sentence: Nobody knows ___ answer to this question.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the phrase 'to this question' identifies exactly which answer we mean, so the noun is specific.
questions.completedSentence: Nobody knows the answer to this question.

questions.sentence: I liked ___ blue shirt in the shop window.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the phrase 'in the shop window' points to one particular shirt that both people can see.
questions.completedSentence: I liked the blue shirt in the shop window.

questions.sentence: My keys are in ___ drawer next to the fridge.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the phrase 'next to the fridge' tells us exactly which drawer we mean.
questions.completedSentence: My keys are in the drawer next to the fridge.

questions.sentence: We had lunch at ___ restaurant we found near the station.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the phrase 'we found near the station' identifies exactly which restaurant we mean.
questions.completedSentence: We had lunch at the restaurant we found near the station.

questions.sentence: The children watched ___ sun go down behind the hills.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because there is only one sun, and nouns for unique things always take 'the'.
questions.completedSentence: The children watched the sun go down behind the hills.

questions.sentence: At night, we can often see ___ moon from our garden.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because we normally see only one moon, so this unique noun always takes 'the'.
questions.completedSentence: At night, we can often see the moon from our garden.

questions.sentence: There is not a single cloud in ___ sky today.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'sky' is a unique noun: there is only one sky above us.
questions.completedSentence: There is not a single cloud in the sky today.

questions.sentence: Millions of people use ___ internet every day.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the internet is one single, unique thing that everyone knows.
questions.completedSentence: Millions of people use the internet every day.

questions.sentence: I bought a book yesterday, and ___ book cost ten euros.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the book was already introduced as 'a book'; on second mention the noun is known information.
questions.completedSentence: I bought a book yesterday, and the book cost ten euros.

questions.sentence: We adopted a cat in May, and ___ cat now sleeps on my bed.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'a cat' introduced the animal first; when we mention it again, it is known to the listener.
questions.completedSentence: We adopted a cat in May, and the cat now sleeps on my bed.

questions.sentence: She made a cake this morning, and ___ cake smells wonderful.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the cake is already known: 'a cake' was mentioned earlier in the same sentence.
questions.completedSentence: She made a cake this morning, and the cake smells wonderful.

questions.sentence: Leo got a bicycle for his birthday, and ___ bicycle is red.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the bicycle was introduced with 'a bicycle'; a repeated, now-known noun takes 'the'.
questions.completedSentence: Leo got a bicycle for his birthday, and the bicycle is red.

questions.sentence: They watched a film last night, but ___ film was quite boring.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because after 'a film' is mentioned, the film becomes known information for the listener.
questions.completedSentence: They watched a film last night, but the film was quite boring.

questions.sentence: There is ___ old bridge at the end of this road.
questions.explanation: Use 'an' because the bridge is mentioned for the first time and is not specific, and 'old' begins with a vowel sound.
questions.completedSentence: There is an old bridge at the end of this road.

questions.sentence: I have ___ idea for our school project.
questions.explanation: Use 'an' because the idea is new to the listener and not specific yet, and 'idea' starts with a vowel sound.
questions.completedSentence: I have an idea for our school project.

questions.sentence: During our trip, we stayed in ___ small hotel near the beach.
questions.explanation: Use 'a' because the hotel is mentioned for the first time, and 'small' starts with a consonant sound.
questions.completedSentence: During our trip, we stayed in a small hotel near the beach.

questions.sentence: The children have ___ breakfast at seven o'clock every day.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'breakfast' is a meal name in a general expression about a daily routine, not one special breakfast.
questions.completedSentence: The children have breakfast at seven o'clock every day.

questions.sentence: After the lesson, we usually have ___ lunch together.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'lunch' refers to the midday meal in general, which is the normal daily routine.
questions.completedSentence: After the lesson, we usually have lunch together.

questions.sentence: Let's meet for ___ dinner on Friday evening.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'dinner' is the normal evening meal in a general arrangement, not a specific special meal.
questions.completedSentence: Let's meet for dinner on Friday evening.

questions.sentence: We play ___ football in the park after class.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'football' is the name of a sport, and sport names take no article in general statements.
questions.completedSentence: We play football in the park after class.

questions.sentence: My friends watch ___ basketball on TV every weekend.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'basketball' is a sport name used in a general sense about a habit.
questions.completedSentence: My friends watch basketball on TV every weekend.

questions.sentence: Her brother is really good at ___ tennis.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'tennis' is the name of a sport, and general sport names after 'good at' take no article.
questions.completedSentence: Her brother is really good at tennis.

questions.sentence: Many people in Egypt speak ___ Arabic at home.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'Arabic' is the name of a language, and language names take no article.
questions.completedSentence: Many people in Egypt speak Arabic at home.

questions.sentence: Is ___ Japanese difficult to learn?
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'Japanese' is a language name, and languages in general statements take no article.
questions.completedSentence: Is Japanese difficult to learn?

questions.sentence: We study ___ English three times a week.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'English' is a school subject and a language name, which take no article in general statements.
questions.completedSentence: We study English three times a week.

questions.sentence: Nowadays, ___ teenagers spend too much time on their phones.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'teenagers' describes the whole group in general, not specific teenagers we know.
questions.completedSentence: Nowadays, teenagers spend too much time on their phones.

questions.sentence: My cousin repairs ___ computers in a small shop.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'computers' means computers in general as part of his job, not particular computers.
questions.completedSentence: My cousin repairs computers in a small shop.

questions.sentence: Hana prefers ___ cats to dogs because they are quieter.
questions.explanation: Use no article because the speaker is comparing cats and dogs as whole categories, and general plural nouns take no article.
questions.completedSentence: Hana prefers cats to dogs because they are quieter.

questions.sentence: Modern cities need ___ parks and green spaces.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'parks' refers to parks in general as a category, not to specific parks.
questions.completedSentence: Modern cities need parks and green spaces.

questions.sentence: Doctors say we should drink ___ water every morning.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'water' is an uncountable noun used in a general sense, meaning water as a substance.
questions.completedSentence: Doctors say we should drink water every morning.

questions.sentence: I never drink ___ coffee after dinner.
questions.explanation: Use no article because coffee in general is an uncountable noun, and no particular coffee is meant here.
questions.completedSentence: I never drink coffee after dinner.

questions.sentence: She relaxes after work by listening to ___ music.
questions.explanation: Use no article because music in general is uncountable; no particular song or album is meant.
questions.completedSentence: She relaxes after work by listening to music.

questions.sentence: My uncle always gives ___ good advice.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'advice' is an uncountable noun used in a general sense, not one specific piece of advice.
questions.completedSentence: My uncle always gives good advice.

questions.sentence: This is ___ best pizza in town.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'best' is a superlative, and superlatives always point to one unmatched thing.
questions.completedSentence: This is the best pizza in town.

questions.sentence: Omar is ___ tallest student in our class.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'tallest' is a superlative describing one unique student, and superlatives require 'the'.
questions.completedSentence: Omar is the tallest student in our class.

questions.sentence: That was ___ most interesting film of the year.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'most interesting' is a superlative form, and superlative expressions always take 'the'.
questions.completedSentence: That was the most interesting film of the year.

questions.sentence: Saturday is ___ busiest day in our shop.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'busiest' is a superlative, and only one day can be the busiest.
questions.completedSentence: Saturday is the busiest day in our shop.

questions.sentence: We live on ___ third floor of an old building.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'third' is an ordinal number marking one definite position in a series, the floors of the building.
questions.completedSentence: We live on the third floor of an old building.

questions.sentence: January is ___ first month of the year.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'first' is an ordinal number marking a definite position in the series of months.
questions.completedSentence: January is the first month of the year.

questions.sentence: He was ___ first person to arrive at the party.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the ordinal 'first' identifies one particular person in a definite order of arrival.
questions.completedSentence: He was the first person to arrive at the party.

questions.sentence: We sat in ___ second row at the cinema.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'second' is an ordinal number identifying the definite row where we sat.
questions.completedSentence: We sat in the second row at the cinema.

questions.sentence: We sailed across ___ Atlantic Ocean on our way to New York.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because names of oceans always take 'the', so we say 'the Atlantic Ocean'.
questions.completedSentence: We sailed across the Atlantic Ocean on our way to New York.

questions.sentence: Many famous buildings stand beside ___ Thames in London.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because river names take 'the', so we say 'the Thames'.
questions.completedSentence: Many famous buildings stand beside the Thames in London.

questions.sentence: Cairo is a huge city on ___ Nile.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because river names take 'the'; the Nile is one specific, well-known river.
questions.completedSentence: Cairo is a huge city on the Nile.

questions.sentence: Tourists swim in ___ Mediterranean Sea all summer.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because sea names take 'the', so we say 'the Mediterranean Sea'.
questions.completedSentence: Tourists swim in the Mediterranean Sea all summer.

questions.sentence: Huge whales travel across ___ Pacific Ocean every year.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because ocean names take 'the', so 'the Pacific Ocean' is correct.
questions.completedSentence: Huge whales travel across the Pacific Ocean every year.

questions.sentence: Please do not drink ___ water in that river.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the phrase 'in that river' tells us exactly which water we mean, so the noun is specific.
questions.completedSentence: Please do not drink the water in that river.

questions.sentence: My brother plays ___ guitar in a local band.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because in standard English, musical instruments take 'the' after 'play', so we say 'play the guitar'.
questions.completedSentence: My brother plays the guitar in a local band.

questions.sentence: She is learning to play ___ piano at school.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because we normally use 'the' with musical instruments like the piano after 'play'.
questions.completedSentence: She is learning to play the piano at school.

questions.sentence: Grandpa plays ___ violin beautifully.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because standard English uses 'the' for musical instruments, so 'plays the violin' is correct.
questions.completedSentence: Grandpa plays the violin beautifully.

questions.sentence: In our school orchestra, I play ___ drums.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because musical instruments take 'the' after 'play', so 'play the drums' is correct.
questions.completedSentence: In our school orchestra, I play the drums.

questions.sentence: Lina has played ___ flute since she was six years old.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because English uses 'the' with musical instruments, so 'has played the flute' is correct.
questions.completedSentence: Lina has played the flute since she was six years old.

questions.sentence: The children walk to ___ school together every morning.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'school' here means the institution and its purpose, attending lessons, not a specific building.
questions.completedSentence: The children walk to school together every morning.

questions.sentence: The students stay in ___ class until half past twelve.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'class' refers to the normal purpose of the institution, having lessons, not a particular room.
questions.completedSentence: The students stay in class until half past twelve.

questions.sentence: My mother is still at ___ work, so we are cooking dinner.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'work' takes no article in the phrase 'at work', which describes the institution's normal purpose, doing a job.
questions.completedSentence: My mother is still at work, so we are cooking dinner.

questions.sentence: The thief was sent to ___ prison for two years.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'prison' refers to the institution's purpose, being held there as a prisoner, not the building itself.
questions.completedSentence: The thief was sent to prison for two years.

questions.sentence: My cousins go to ___ church every Sunday.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'church' means attending a religious service, the institution's purpose, not one specific building.
questions.completedSentence: My cousins go to church every Sunday.

questions.sentence: My brother adopted ___ puppy from the animal shelter.
questions.explanation: Use 'a' because the puppy is mentioned for the first time and 'puppy' starts with a consonant sound.
questions.completedSentence: My brother adopted a puppy from the animal shelter.

questions.sentence: She carried ___ enormous suitcase up the stairs.
questions.explanation: Use 'an' because 'enormous' begins with a vowel sound, and the suitcase is new to the listener.
questions.completedSentence: She carried an enormous suitcase up the stairs.

questions.sentence: Mr. Hill works as ___ taxi driver in Madrid.
questions.explanation: Use 'a' because 'taxi driver' is a job, and 'taxi' starts with a consonant sound.
questions.completedSentence: Mr. Hill works as a taxi driver in Madrid.

questions.sentence: One day, I want to become ___ astronaut.
questions.explanation: Use 'an' because 'astronaut' is a job that begins with a vowel sound.
questions.completedSentence: One day, I want to become an astronaut.

questions.sentence: My sister practises ___ cello every evening.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because musical instruments take 'the' after 'practise', just like after 'play'.
questions.completedSentence: My sister practises the cello every evening.

questions.sentence: Our teacher plays ___ saxophone in a jazz band.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because in standard English, musical instruments take 'the' after 'play'.
questions.completedSentence: Our teacher plays the saxophone in a jazz band.

questions.sentence: After the accident, she spent a week in ___ hospital.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'hospital' refers to the institution's purpose, receiving treatment, not a specific building.
questions.completedSentence: After the accident, she spent a week in hospital.

questions.sentence: The whole family goes to ___ bed before ten o'clock.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'go to bed' describes the purpose of sleeping, not a particular bed.
questions.completedSentence: The whole family goes to bed before ten o'clock.

questions.sentence: Please close ___ window next to the door.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'next to the door' identifies exactly which window the speaker means.
questions.completedSentence: Please close the window next to the door.

questions.sentence: Could you turn off ___ light above the sink?
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because 'above the sink' points to one specific light.
questions.completedSentence: Could you turn off the light above the sink?

questions.sentence: We watched ___ moon rise over the mountains.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the moon is treated as a unique thing that everyone can identify.
questions.completedSentence: We watched the moon rise over the mountains.

questions.sentence: Plants need light from ___ sun to grow.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because the sun is a unique thing known to everyone.
questions.completedSentence: Plants need light from the sun to grow.

questions.sentence: We eat ___ breakfast at seven every morning.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'breakfast' names a routine meal in a general expression.
questions.completedSentence: We eat breakfast at seven every morning.

questions.sentence: Our family usually has ___ dinner together on Fridays.
questions.explanation: Use no article because 'dinner' is the name of a meal used in a routine expression.
questions.completedSentence: Our family usually has dinner together on Fridays.

questions.sentence: Nadia plays ___ tennis after school.
questions.explanation: Use no article because names of sports such as tennis normally take no article.
questions.completedSentence: Nadia plays tennis after school.

questions.sentence: My friends play ___ basketball every weekend.
questions.explanation: Use no article because basketball is the name of a sport.
questions.completedSentence: My friends play basketball every weekend.
